page: Microsoft Azure D128nds_v6 is a General Purpose virtual machine within the Dndv6 family, powered by Intel x86_64 architecture on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 128 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual processor core. It integrates 7560 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage disks, while omitting discrete GPU acceleration.

The inclusion of 7560 GB of fast local NVMe SSD media gives this configuration high-throughput local scratch capability, complementing its network optimization capabilities for communication-heavy operations. Infrastructure deployment does not allocate default complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Compute capability is provided across the full 128 dedicated x86_64 execution threads, making it capable of handling large multithreaded task sets without hardware accelerator dependencies.

By pairing a balanced memory profile with substantial local storage density, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for resource-heavy workloads that would otherwise require multiple smaller virtual machines or separate high-performance storage arrays. The main architectural tradeoff involves reliance on ephemeral local storage rather than persistent clustered disks for the local NVMe space. This hardware profile is appropriate for large-scale enterprise databases, distributed caching layers, ETL pipelines, software build environments, and data analysis jobs requiring extensive local caching.
description: Microsoft Azure D128nds_v6 is a high-density General Purpose virtual machine within the Dndv6 family, powered by Intel x86_64 architecture running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 128 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture is anchored by 7560 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD space alongside Premium Storage compatibility and network optimization capabilities, while operating without discrete GPU accelerators. By pairing substantial multi-core compute capacity with an expansive high-speed local disk footprint, the instance eliminates local storage bottlenecks for I/O-intensive services. This configuration delivers cost-efficient hardware utilization for consolidated enterprise environments, large distributed caching systems, high-concurrency relational and NoSQL databases, and intensive batch processing or ETL workloads requiring vast scratch space.
